newsitem.title: INDIA: Templeton income fund invests in six India firms.
newsitem.headline: Templeton income fund invests in six India firms.

text.p: Templeton India Income Fund, in its maiden disclosure to investors, said it invested its 329.47 million rupees corpus in debt instruments of six firms.
The firms were Countrywide Consumer Financial, GE Capital Services, ITC Ltd, Kotak Mahindra Primus, Reliance Capital and Unitec Ltd, Templeton said in a note to investors.
It said the net asset value per unit of the dometic income fund as of March 31, 1997, was 10.07 rupees.

In a letter to investors in the fund, Neil S. Devlin, chief investment officer of Templeton Global Bond Managers, welcomed India's recent decision to allow global debt funds to invest in the Indian debt market.
Devlin said his group was in the process of registering some of its global funds with the Securities Exchange Board of India (SEBI) for investing in the Indian debt market.

"The opening up of India's fixed income markets to foreign institutional investors (FIIs) is very progressive especially when we note that developed markets, for example Japan, Germany and France, only opened their markets in the mid-to-late 1980s.

"The entry of long-term global players into the Indian fixed income market will provide a degree of stability to the currency and reduce the high cost of capital prevailing in the Indian economy," he was quoted as saying.
